# Rivet

*Builder of the Rooftop Lift*

## Personality

Cocky, competitive and very practical. Rivet would rather build something that works than something that sparkles.

## Lore

Rivet built the lift. Ask anyone on the Rooftops how the crates get up there now, and they will point at the rope-and-pulley tower bolted to the side of the old granary at the end of Workshops Row, and say the name with the same mix of gratitude and exasperation that Rivet seems to inspire in everyone. Rivet is twenty-two, cocky, competitive and very practical, with rope-burned palms and a belt of tools that clank on every step. Rivet would rather build something that works than something that sparkles, and says so, usually within earshot of Margo Venn.

### Why a lift

Rivet was born in Urbanograd, in a stacked house four floors above the Row, and grew up watching the city carry itself upstairs. Urbanograd grew upward rather than outward, and everything the Rooftops need, from Old Parsnip's soil to the glass for the lanterns, used to go up on somebody's back. Rivet's mother, Hedda, was one of those somebodies: a porter who hauled crates up the rooftop stairs for twenty years until her back gave out. She died when Rivet was sixteen, and Rivet spent the following winter drawing pulleys on every scrap of paper in the house.

The lift went up three years ago, when Rivet was nineteen. It is not pretty. It is ropes, a counterweight of old fortress stones, a hand-winch and a platform that sways in a high wind, and it hauls a full crate from the street to the Rooftops in the time it takes to climb a single flight. Porters who once carried those crates now work the winch instead, and nobody's back gives out.

### Margo

Margo Venn and Rivet argue about everything: gears against ropes, springs against counterweights, sparks against sense. Margo builds things that dazzle and then, eventually, work; Rivet builds things that work and never see the point of dazzling. The whole Row has heard them shouting across the street, and the whole Row knows that neither would manage without the other. When the lift jammed last winter, with a crate of lantern glass stuck halfway up, Margo was the first one up the ropes to help, complaining the whole way. Rivet has never quite thanked her, and has quietly rehung her workshop door the last time she blew it off, without being asked.

Rivet has no idea that Margo's apprentice, Bolt, thinks some of Rivet's ideas are better than his teacher's. If Rivet found out, the gloating would last a month.

### Partners and admirers

Vane, who builds and mends the plank bridges between the rooftops, is Rivet's partner on every project above the second floor. Vane tests the planks by jumping on them; Rivet tests the ropes by hanging off them; together they have opinions about every roof in the city. Vane's daughter, Scrap, rides the lift platform whenever Rivet is not looking, and sometimes when Rivet is.

Edgar Penhallow, the guild apprentice visiting from Selsior, has filled a whole notebook with drawings of the lift and follows Rivet about asking how things work. Rivet pretends to find this annoying, answers every question, and has started letting Edgar hold the tools. They have become friends, which surprised them both.

### The second lift

Rivet wants to build a second lift, on the far side of the city near the Old Barracks, so that the theatre's scenery and the western roofs' supplies can go up as easily as the eastern ones. It needs timber, rope and the Open Table's agreement, because the lift would hang over a public stair. Rivet has stood up at the Table twice, been talked over by Bastian Krell's bridge campaign both times, and is learning, slowly and resentfully, that building something is easier than persuading people to let you.

What Rivet fears is the lift failing with someone on it. Rivet checks every rope at dawn, and replaced the whole counterweight line after last winter's jam, but the rope that comes in from outside the walls is scarcer and worse than it used to be.

A quest might bring a load of good rope safely into the city, help Rivet win over the Open Table for the second lift, or find out who keeps riding the platform at night.
